messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT: prod-region-3/runtime OOM surge — high paging detected on inference pool rwd-infer-3. Auto-scale failed to recover. Alert: 60% of hosts reporting >90% GPU memory fragmentation. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/rwd/oom-rt?orgId=1
Maya P: acknowledged. I'm taking pager. starting live triage. tagging eng-sre and runtime.
Dmitri K: on standby. initial ask: can we get the last 20m of per-GPU alloc metrics + KV cache size timeline (per host)?
Eng-SRE-Bot: logs bucket created: s3://rwd-incident-4975312468/logs/ — contains dmesg, runtime-alloc-trace, kvcache-stats.
Ben J: copying a quick snapshot from host rwd-infer-3-12:```
GPU0 total: 48GB
GPU0 used: 46.8GB
GPU0 free: 1.2GB
KVCache size: 10.2GB
KVCache entries: 1.3M
Fragmentation metric: 0.82
Last GC: 2026-03-17T02:18:44Z
```
Carla S: hmm KVCache 10GB is big for this tenant mix. which model var? looks like mpt-30b-8bit pinned.
Dmitri K: hypothesis A: prefix-heavy requests caused unbounded KV growth -> page churn -> fragmentation -> OOM under normal batching. Hypothesis B: sudden batch size spike combined with a kernel memory leak.
Maya P: immediate mitigations: 1) reduce default batch_size to 1 on affected pool (done for rwd-infer-3-*) 2) enable aggressive kvcache-eviction (LRU trim to 2GB) 3) temporarily disable persistent prefix-cache for long-running sessions. please ack when applied.
Ben J: applied batch_size=1 on pool via deploy flag. change rolled to 6/8 hosts.
Eng-SRE-Bot: kvcache eviction policy changed to trim_threshold=2GB at 4975312540 (applied to hosts: 3-8).
Maya P: good. what's customer impact right now? Support Ops?
Support Ops: triage inbound — 3 customers reported errors in last 30m (tickets #INC-1823, #INC-1824, #INC-1825). Errors: 503s and truncated responses. No data exfiltration. We pushed a banner to status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/4975312468
Eva L: starting timeline doc: https://docs.redwood.internal/incident-4975312468 — adding events. request everyone to paste short entries with UTC times.
Dmitri K: adding hypothesis notes and requested logs to doc. also uploading `nvml_top` dumps to the bucket.
Ben J: still seeing a tail of long requests — suspect long context sessions keeping KV pinned. we should correlate session ids to KV growth.
Carla S: quick grep of kvcache-stats shows many entries with ttl=null and large prefix tokens. might be a bug in session garbage collection. adding to hypotheses.
Maya P: next actions: a) keep batch_size=1 until further notice; b) run KV sweep job to forcibly evict entries older than 5m from this pool (run id: sweep-4975312600) c) collect per-tenant session id list for the 3 impacted customers.
Eng-SRE-Bot: sweep job started at 4975312600, hosts affected: 3-8. progress: 0/6 -> 6/6, evicted ~7.8GB total KV across pool.
Ben J: after sweep, free memory on sampled host rwd-infer-3-12 went from 1.2GB -> 12.6GB. fragmentation metric dropped to 0.46. latency improved for small requests.
Maya P: great. please keep the customer comms updated. Support Ops, any customers still erroring?
Support Ops: last update: #INC-1824 still seeing occasional 503s but volume down 92% since mitigations. informing customers of temporary limits/backoff recommendations.
Dmitri K: logging/diagnostics to capture for RCA: per-gpu vmmap snapshots, allocator logs, kernel mem stats, kvcache growth traces, batch size distribution. please preserve artifacts and mark as high-priority.
Carla S: also note we turned off persistent prefix caching for this pool at 4975312625 — adding config diff to doc.
Maya P: labeling this incident: root candidates: unbounded KV growth + session GC bug -> fragmentation -> OOM during normal batching. mitigation worked (eviction + batch reduction).
Eva L: starting RCA notes in doc, collecting owner assignments. Action items: runtime: fix session GC + cap kvcache by default. infra: add eviction circuit-breaker and an alert for kvcache absolute size per host. SRE: consider auto-downgrade of batch_size at threshold.
Maya P: thanks team. I'll hand off to post-incident and schedule follow-up retro. leaving this thread open for additional logs. :thumbsup:
